probability noun

likelihood

also likelihood, probable, plausibility, chance (likelihood), in all probability

classical

Cic. Ac. 2.75 (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Tusc. 5.33
M-O s.v. probability (mathematics: Gauss)

probābilitās, probābilitātis f.

noun, third declension

probability, likelihood, credibility

Cicero’s word, in the sense of the Academic philosophers: how likely or believable a thing is. The mathematicians kept it for probability as a measure. For “probably, in all probability” in speech, see probably (opīnor, vērī simile est).

Other words

  • vērī similitūdō, vērī similitūdinis f. — likelihood, probability (“likeness to the truth”)

    also used · classical · Cic. Ac. 2.107: ipsam vērī similitūdinem … sequī; Cic. Part. 40: similitūdō vērī

    Often written as one word, vērīsimilitūdō; the adjective is vērī similis, likely.

Examples

  • quodcumque nostrōs animōs probābilitāte percussit, id dīcimus

    whatever has struck our minds as probable, that is what we sayCic. Tusc. 5.33

See also probably, possibility.
